name: math_boundary_operator

phase_0.boundary_condition: The nilpotency condition where the square of the boundary operator equals zero

VINIT.justification: The trivial module serves as the initial object and the starting point for any chain construction.

TANCH.justification: The requirement that the composition of two boundary maps vanishes defines the boundary of the entire algebraic system.

AFWD.justification: The boundary operator acts as a forward morphism mapping an n-chain to an (n-1)-chain.

AREV.justification: The coboundary operator acts as the contravariant partner mapping an n-cochain to an (n+1)-cochain.

CLINK.justification: Sequential application of boundary operators forms the chain complex structure.

IMSCRIB.justification: The identity map on a module ensures self-recognition of the algebraic structure within the complex.

FSPLIT.justification: The boundary operator splits the module into the kernel of the current map and the image of the preceding map.

FFUSE.justification: The direct sum of the kernel and its complement reconstitutes the original module space.

EVALT.justification: An element is a cycle if its boundary is zero, representing a successful affirmative evaluation.

EVALF.justification: An element is not a cycle if its boundary is non-zero, representing a negative evaluation.

ENGAGR.justification: Every boundary is a cycle but not every cycle is a boundary, creating a state where an element holds both identities until homology is computed.

IFIX.justification: The quotient of the kernel by the image creates a permanent, invariant record of the topological hole.

phase_3.void_description: The empty set of chains before any boundary maps are defined
phase_3.true_description: The element belongs to the kernel of the boundary operator
phase_3.false_description: The element does not belong to the kernel of the boundary operator
phase_3.both_description: The element is simultaneously a cycle and a boundary within the homology group

steps.domain_action: Establish the zero module as the basis for the chain complex
Identify the module M_n at the current dimension
Decompose M_n into potential cycles and non-cycles
Filter for elements in the kernel where d(x) = 0
Apply the boundary operator d_n to map M_n to M_n-1
Record the image of the boundary operator in M_n-1
Recombine the kernel and image components to verify module integrity
Compose d_n with d_n-1 to test for nilpotency
Branch the composition into the zero map and non-zero remainders
Identify any non-zero results that violate the chain complex definition
Map back via the dual coboundary to verify adjoint consistency
Reconstitute the sequence into a single chain complex object
Hold the cycle and boundary identities in tension to define homology
Fix the homology group H_n as the permanent invariant of the system
Seal the complex under the global d^2 = 0 boundary condition

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The functor that maps topological spaces to algebraic chain complexes
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The exact sequences that communicate information between adjacent modules
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The graded module structure that stores chains of different dimensions
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The indexing of the chain complex which determines the order of map application
phase_5.alfs_store: The Eilenberg-Steenrod axioms providing the bootstrap for homology theory

phase_6.cycle_cost: The algebraic reduction required to compute the quotient group
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A collection of modules and arbitrary linear maps
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A structured chain complex with defined homology invariants
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The information lost during the quotient process is preserved in the definition of the homology classes.
